note: X prints one message of the getTemp process: 128 samples in kelvin x 100. The host suite (Tools/Developer/tests/cli/port/test_x.c) owns the error paths - a missing, killed or failing producer - which the board can reach only by killing getTemp, and that cannot be undone without a reset. These rows prove what the real producer and the real kernel mailbox deliver.

tests.note: exactly KNB_SAMPLES (128) values after the 'x' tag, on one line; X waits up to 10 s for a message and getTemp sends one every 200 ms
every sample in 29319..29949: getTemp's simulated table (20.03..23.78 degC + 273.16) x 100 plus 0..255 of noise. getTemp simulates wherever the variant builds no temperature manager

with a temperature manager (Alastor_H743: the LSM9DS1) getTemp reads the sensor: kelvin x 100, every sample in 27800..33299 (4.8..60.1 degC). A value near 57000 or 0 means the kelvin offset was added twice or the history holds heap garbage. 128 x 29809 is raw -1 (-1/16 + 25 + 273.16 K): the SPI read returned all ones, i.e. the chip did not answer
pins CURRENT behaviour: prgm() never looks at argc, so the console's three tokens are ignored. The host test x_takes_no_arguments cannot see the console's split
the mailbox handle is looked up once per core and cached; each read frees the producer's buffer. A lost handle answers 'mbox problem', a leak shows up in health-after once the heap runs out

expect: ^(The process Temperature was killed!|Process Temperature not installed!)$

tests.poisons: getTemp is gone until the next reset; X answers 'not installed'
tests.note: getTemp must exit on its own within two sample periods even with a full mailbox (it used to block in kern_writeMailbox until a reader drained a message), and X must report the producer gone without logging an error. The one-second pause lets it exit before X asks; a cached handle then answers 'was killed', an uncached one 'not installed'
